controls.title: Authenticated-by-default routed endpoints
controls.invariant: A routed endpoint without authorization metadata requires an authenticated user; public access needs explicit anonymous metadata.

enforcement.description: Authenticated-user fallback authorization policy

controls.operationalDependency: A configured sign-in provider or host-owned identity flow. The default scaffold has none, so protected routes stay unavailable until one is added.

failure.detail: Unannotated routed endpoints reject anonymous users. The --authProvider none scaffold and RequireAuthenticatedUserByDefault=false are explicit opt-outs that make unannotated endpoints public.

controls.hostResponsibility: Configure the identity provider, review and test every anonymous exception, and authorize access to business resources and operations.
controls.nonClaims: Requires an authenticated identity; it does not decide whether that identity may act on a specific resource. Named role and permission policies apply only where an endpoint declares them.

controls.title: Governance policy evaluation
controls.invariant: A governance decision reflects every registered constraint, and a denial from any constraint wins.

enforcement.description: Default governance policy evaluator

controls.operationalDependency: Host-registered constraints, threat contributors, and decision policy.

failure.detail: An empty constraint set denies by default (DenyWhenNoConstraints), and constraint and threat-contributor exceptions become denials by default. Both defaults can be switched off; the permissive empty-policy path then only logs a warning.

controls.hostResponsibility: Register constraints that express the real policy, and keep the fail-closed defaults unless a documented lower-risk exception applies.
controls.nonClaims: A decision is only as complete as the registered constraints. Endpoint policy markers do not select or derive constraints; every registered constraint runs on every governed endpoint.

controls.title: Decision before execution at the HTTP edge
controls.invariant: A governed endpoint executes only after an allowing decision; denied, unverified, or misconfigured requests do not reach the endpoint.

enforcement.description: Endpoint governance middleware, registered after routing and authentication

controls.operationalDependency: Correct middleware order and a registered policy evaluator.

failure.detail: The middleware blocks the endpoint with a safe HTTP result when policy, capability, or configuration checks fail. Invalid endpoint-governance options fail at startup through options validation.

controls.hostResponsibility: Gate every non-HTTP path yourself (background jobs, message consumers, internal services, CLI tools), place side effects below the decision check, and treat a missing decision or failed evaluation as a denial on consequential paths.
controls.nonClaims: Protects only the HTTP endpoints where the middleware is registered. AsiBackbone does not execute operations and cannot make a host honor a decision.

controls.title: Acknowledgment challenge before continuation
controls.invariant: An acknowledgment-required decision answers with a challenge and does not execute until an acknowledged retry is evaluated again.

enforcement.description: Acknowledgment challenge service

controls.operationalDependency: Host storage for acknowledgment requests and responses, linked to decision and lifecycle evidence.

failure.detail: The challenged request does not execute. A valid capability grant never upgrades an acknowledgment-required decision, so a grant cannot bypass the challenge.

controls.hostResponsibility: Authenticate and authorize the acknowledging actor, present the acknowledgment accessibly, define when acknowledgment is required, choose storage and retention, and decide freshness rules before execution.
controls.nonClaims: Records an acknowledgment checkpoint. It is not legal protection, non-repudiation, compliance certification, or production tamper-evidence, and an acknowledgment record is not an execution credential.

controls.title: Signed capability grants and replay protection
controls.invariant: A signed capability grant authorizes one bound request for one subject, operation, scope, and policy, and cannot be replayed beyond its use limit.

enforcement.description: Capability grant validator with a capability-grant use store

controls.operationalDependency: A verification service, a request binding provider, and a durable use store shared by every replica, with expired records purged on a schedule.

failure.detail: The signed endpoint validator denies every result other than Valid, including results the core validator would defer or escalate. A missing verification service, use store, or binding provider denies, as does one that throws. Grants are single-use by default.

controls.hostResponsibility: Own key material and the verification service, the use store and its migration and purge, issuer and audience expectations, clock skew, and what a request binding covers.
controls.nonClaims: Signed grants are opt-in; the default claim-backed validator has no replay semantics. Replay protection is only as wide as the use store: the in-memory store is process-local, so behind a load balancer a single-use grant can be accepted once per replica.

controls.title: Decision evidence persistence
controls.invariant: Governance decision receipts are persisted to the host database before the governed operation executes.

enforcement.description: EF Core audit ledger store on a host-owned DbContext

controls.operationalDependency: A host-owned DbContext, database provider, and applied migrations that include the AsiBackbone tables.

failure.detail: Whether a failed append blocks execution is decided by the host's decision receipt sink. In the Reference Application a failed append throws, so the governed operation fails closed, and governed operations fail closed until the migration is applied.

controls.hostResponsibility: Own the DbContext, connection, migrations, transactions, retention, and backups, and make the receipt sink fail closed on consequential paths.
controls.nonClaims: Ledger rows are not immutable or tamper-evident by themselves. Tamper-evidence needs signing or hash-chain verification plus protected storage and retention controls.

controls.title: Application mutation audit manifest digest
controls.invariant: A retained audit batch can be checked against the receipt issued when the mutation was saved.

enforcement.description: Canonical mutation manifest verifier with a fixed-time digest comparison

controls.operationalDependency: Retained audit batches and their receipts.

failure.detail: Verification succeeds only when the retained batch still matches the receipt's manifest and record count. The caller decides what a mismatch blocks.

controls.hostResponsibility: Retain batches and receipts, run verification where it matters, and supply transaction strategy, access controls, retention, immutable storage, and signing or timestamping where required.
controls.nonClaims: The default digest is an unkeyed SHA-256 hash, so it detects change but not a rewrite by someone who can also replace the stored digest. A match does not prove an atomic commit, immutable storage, retention compliance, an authenticated actor or upstream decision, or a complete archive transfer.

controls.title: Governance outbox delivery
controls.invariant: Governance emissions are saved locally before downstream delivery, and delivery failures are preserved as outbox state.

enforcement.description: Provider-neutral governance outbox drain

controls.operationalDependency: A durable outbox store, a drain worker, and an emission provider.

failure.detail: Provider failures become retryable, deferred, failed, or dead-lettered outbox state; the local record is kept for review and retry.

controls.hostResponsibility: Own worker topology, claim and lease behavior, provider idempotency, migrations, duplicate reconciliation, retention, and monitoring.
controls.nonClaims: Not a distributed queue, an append-only event stream, or an immutable ledger. Delivery is at-least-once and best-effort; exactly-once delivery is not claimed.

controls.title: Audit completion outbox and reconciliation
controls.invariant: A committed mutation's audit completion is handed off durably, and missing, altered, or stalled evidence is detected afterwards.

enforcement.description: Optional audit completion outbox, with a scheduled reconciler

controls.operationalDependency: The outbox and reconciliation features enabled, the application database, and an optional external publisher.

failure.detail: With no publisher, ready entries are deferred rather than failing the business mutation. Retryable failures back off and dead-letter after MaxRetryAttempts. Reconciliation findings surface through the audit-integrity health check, which is kept out of readiness.

controls.hostResponsibility: Make publishers idempotent on the idempotency key, and review and remediate reconciliation findings.
controls.nonClaims: A durable local handoff, not a distributed queue; exactly-once delivery is not promised. Reconciliation detects problems after the transaction; it does not replace transactional persistence.

controls.title: Signature verification policy
controls.invariant: Only a valid signature from a trusted key and signing context is accepted.

enforcement.description: Verification policy evaluator

controls.operationalDependency: A verification provider, key lookup, and trust pins for keys and signing context.

failure.detail: Only Valid allows by default. Hash mismatches, untrusted keys, and untrusted signing contexts deny; an unknown key version escalates and an unavailable provider defers.

controls.hostResponsibility: Provide the signing and verification infrastructure, configure key and context pins, and map deferred or escalated results to execution decisions.
controls.nonClaims: A valid signature shows the payload matches what the key signed. It does not prove legal non-repudiation, immutable storage, or that the signer was authorized to act.

controls.title: Audit-integrity hash chain
controls.invariant: Changed, missing, reordered, or forked audit records are detected when the chain is verified.

enforcement.description: Audit integrity verifier

controls.operationalDependency: Retained chain metadata stored next to the audit records, and a process that runs verification.

failure.detail: Verification reports categorized failures such as a previous-link hash mismatch. The host decides what a failure blocks and how it is escalated.

controls.hostResponsibility: Persist link metadata, run verification on a schedule or before reliance, and protect chain tips, for example in immutable storage.
controls.nonClaims: A local hash chain detects change only when verified against retained metadata. It is not tamper-evident without protected storage, external anchoring, and retention controls, and it is not a blockchain or transparency log.

controls.title: Production signing-key custody
controls.invariant: Production private keys stay in a host-controlled key-management system and never pass through AsiBackbone.

enforcement.description: Host-owned managed-key signing client behind the AsiBackbone managed-key adapter

controls.evidenceGap: Custody evidence is deployment-specific. These tests cover the adapter boundary and the Reference Application's startup key checks, not any production key-management system.
controls.operationalDependency: A cloud KMS, HSM, or organization signing service reachable from the host.

failure.detail: An unavailable signing provider maps to a deferral or retry for lower-risk work and should fail closed for high-risk execution. The Reference Application fails startup when its signing key does not match a trusted, unrevoked verification key.

controls.hostResponsibility: Choose and operate the key-management system, control access to keys, rotate and revoke key versions, and distribute public verification keys.
controls.nonClaims: AsiBackbone is not a key-management system: it ships no first-party cloud KMS or HSM provider, automatic rotation, or emergency revocation. The Reference Application's configured PEM key is a sample, not production custody.

controls.title: ASP.NET Core Data Protection key ring
controls.invariant: Every replica protects and unprotects cookies and antiforgery tokens with the same persisted key ring.

enforcement.description: Data Protection registration and startup posture checks

controls.operationalDependency: Durable, access-restricted key-ring storage shared by every replica, and an optional key-encryption certificate.

failure.detail: Startup fails when the key-encryption certificate is missing, has no private key, or a password is set without a certificate path. Outside Development, warnings 1003 (relative key-ring path) and 1004 (unencrypted key ring) flag common deployment problems without stopping startup.

controls.hostResponsibility: Provide durable shared storage, use one ApplicationName per application, encrypt the key ring, and keep retired certificates available until their keys age out.
controls.nonClaims: Without a key-encryption certificate or storage-level encryption, key-ring files are stored unencrypted by the application.

controls.title: Reverse-proxy and TLS trust
controls.invariant: Client address and scheme come only from forwarded headers sent by an explicitly trusted proxy or network.

enforcement.description: Forwarded-headers configuration with a startup trust check

controls.operationalDependency: The deployment's proxy, ingress, or load balancer topology, and TLS termination.

failure.detail: Outside Development, startup fails when forwarded client-IP processing and rate limiting are active without a KnownProxies or KnownNetworks entry. Raw X-Forwarded-For values are never trusted directly.

controls.hostResponsibility: Terminate TLS and manage certificates, configure the narrowest trusted proxy addresses or networks (replace the sample Kubernetes range), and set AllowedHosts if X-Forwarded-Host is enabled.
controls.nonClaims: An over-broad trusted network lets clients spoof their address. The template cannot know the deployment's proxy topology.

controls.title: Request rate limiting
controls.invariant: Clients are rate limited per resolved address, and unresolved clients remain limited.

enforcement.description: Fixed-window and concurrency rate limiters

controls.operationalDependency: Correct proxy trust, so the client address is the real client rather than the ingress.

failure.detail: By default, clients without a resolved address share one fallback partition and stay rate limited, with warning 6002 when that path is used. Rejections are inexpensive 429 responses.

controls.hostResponsibility: Tune limits for real traffic, and provide edge or distributed rate limiting and denial-of-service protection where needed.
controls.nonClaims: The limiter keeps its counters in each application instance's memory, so limits apply per replica rather than across a scaled deployment. It is not denial-of-service protection.

controls.title: Health and readiness endpoints
controls.invariant: Probes report liveness and readiness without login state and without exposing sensitive diagnostics.

enforcement.description: Anonymous health, readiness, liveness, and audit-integrity endpoints

controls.operationalDependency: The application database for readiness when data access is enabled.

failure.detail: Readiness fails when the database is unreachable, liveness has no dependency checks, and audit integrity is kept out of readiness. In Production, a startup warning names the anonymously mapped health routes.

controls.hostResponsibility: Restrict health endpoint reachability at the deployment boundary, and register any further dependency checks that define readiness for the service.
controls.nonClaims: Anonymous mapping does not mean the endpoints should be reachable from the Internet. Responses must not carry secrets, configuration, or exception details.

controls.title: Database migrations and provider support
controls.invariant: Schema changes are applied as an explicit, reviewed deployment step, never automatically at startup.

enforcement.description: Data-access startup diagnostic and explicit migration commands

controls.operationalDependency: A supported provider (SQLite or SQL Server) and a deployment step that applies migrations.

failure.detail: The application never migrates at startup. A SQL Server scaffold ships without migration history and logs a warning with the command to create one.

controls.hostResponsibility: Generate, review, and apply provider-specific migrations, including the AsiBackbone tables, and back up the database before schema changes.
controls.nonClaims: Providers other than SQLite and SQL Server are not supported. Generated migrations are not reviewed by the template; their correctness for the selected provider is the host's to check.

controls.title: Development-only plain-HTTP cookie override
controls.invariant: Authentication cookies are sent over HTTP only in Development.

enforcement.description: Authentication options validation at startup

controls.operationalDependency: An accurate hosting environment name.

failure.detail: Startup validation rejects AllowInsecureHttp=true in every environment other than Development.

controls.hostResponsibility: Keep the override in Development-only configuration sources, and make sure deployed environments never run as Development.
controls.nonClaims: The guard trusts the environment name; a deployment that runs as Development disables it.

controls.title: Local-development signing kept out of production
controls.invariant: The local-development signing provider is not registered in a production environment.

enforcement.description: Registration-time production guard, backed by analyzers ASIB002 and ASIB003

controls.operationalDependency: An accurate hosting environment name, and analyzers enabled in the build.

failure.detail: Registering the provider in a production environment throws unless AllowInProduction is set. The analyzers warn at build time by default.

controls.hostResponsibility: Elevate ASIB002 and ASIB003 to errors in production CI, and never set AllowInProduction.
controls.nonClaims: The provider generates a new key in each process by default; its signatures are not production evidence.

controls.title: Reference Application demo identity
controls.invariant: The demonstration sign-in and its fixed claims exist only in Development.

enforcement.description: Environment-gated service and endpoint registration

controls.operationalDependency: An accurate hosting environment name.

failure.detail: Outside the Development environment neither the service nor the sign-in endpoint is registered, even when the switch is set. A startup warning is written whenever the control is active.

controls.hostResponsibility: Do not carry the demonstration identity into a derived application.
controls.nonClaims: A demonstration aid, not an identity provider; its fixed claims prove nothing about a real user.

controls.title: NCAT release provenance and SBOM evidence
controls.invariant: Each tagged release publishes a durable, hashed evidence set for the exact NuGet package and container image.

enforcement.description: Tag-driven publish workflows that generate evidence before publication

controls.operationalDependency: GitHub Actions OIDC, artifact attestations, keyless image signing, and the protected publishing environment.

failure.detail: The publish workflow fails when the GitHub release is missing a required evidence asset.

controls.hostResponsibility: Verify the evidence manifest hashes, SBOMs, provenance attestations, and image signature before relying on a release.
controls.nonClaims: NuGet author signing is deferred (ADR-0005). SBOMs and provenance describe how an artifact was built; they do not show it is free of vulnerabilities.

controls.title: AsiBackbone package provenance and SBOM evidence
controls.invariant: Each stable release attaches attested packages, SBOMs, release notes, and a checksum manifest to the GitHub release.

enforcement.description: Package publish workflow

controls.operationalDependency: GitHub Actions artifact attestations where the workflow event supports them.

failure.detail: The release workflow verifies every required release asset and package attestation.

controls.hostResponsibility: Verify package hashes, SBOMs, and attestations before adopting a release.
controls.nonClaims: NuGet package signing is deferred for the 7.x line under a time-bounded decision record. SBOMs and provenance do not make the packages a compliance product.

controls.title: NCAT repository rulesets and security scanning
controls.invariant: Changes reach main only through pull requests that pass the required checks and code-scanning thresholds.

enforcement.description: Main branch ruleset, recorded as a desired-state manifest

controls.operationalDependency: GitHub-hosted settings, which live outside git.

failure.detail: The read-only drift audit exits nonzero on required drift and reports administrator-only controls as Unavailable rather than compliant.

controls.hostResponsibility: Run the audit with an administrator login before each stable release, and change the manifest and live setting together.
controls.nonClaims: The audit detects drift; it never changes settings. Settings it cannot read are unverified, not compliant.

controls.title: AsiBackbone repository rulesets and security scanning
controls.invariant: Changes reach main only through pull requests that pass release-blocking CI.

enforcement.description: Main branch ruleset, recorded as a desired-state manifest

controls.evidenceGap: No scheduled workflow compares the live ruleset with the manifest; that depends on a maintainer running the script with administrator access.
controls.operationalDependency: GitHub-hosted settings, which live outside git.

failure.detail: The ruleset blocks merges that skip required checks. Emergency bypass is limited to one maintainer and to pull requests.

controls.hostResponsibility: Apply manifest changes deliberately; the script changes GitHub settings only when run with -Apply.
controls.nonClaims: The manifest records intent; without a scheduled comparison, drift between it and the live ruleset is not detected automatically.

controls.title: Reference Application repository rulesets
controls.invariant: Changes reach main only through pull requests that pass every CI job, and reach ncat-baseline only through pull requests.

enforcement.description: Main and ncat-baseline branch rulesets, recorded as desired-state manifests

controls.evidenceGap: The tests check the committed manifests against the CI workflows; nothing compares them with the live rulesets.
controls.operationalDependency: GitHub-hosted settings, which live outside git.

failure.detail: The rulesets block merges that skip a required CI job, and the tests fail when the manifest stops requiring a CI job.

controls.hostResponsibility: Change the manifest and live rulesets together.
controls.nonClaims: The manifests record intent; live drift is not detected automatically.

controls.title: Organization repository rulesets and security scanning
controls.invariant: Changes to organization defaults, standards, and this map reach main only through pull requests that pass the required checks and CodeQL thresholds.

enforcement.description: Main branch security baseline ruleset, recorded as a desired-state manifest

controls.evidenceGap: No drift audit compares the ruleset manifest with the live ruleset.
controls.operationalDependency: GitHub-hosted settings, which live outside git.

failure.detail: The ruleset requires three status checks and CodeQL code-scanning results on every pull request. Path-filtered and scheduled checks are deliberately not required.

controls.hostResponsibility: Change the manifest and live ruleset together.
controls.nonClaims: The manifest records intent; live drift is not detected automatically.
